title: Coefficient-natural higher-direct-image comparison with a resolution formula
statement: Let f:X→Y be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], p∈ℕ, and put U=f⁻¹(V) for an open V of Y. Use module cohomology and ordinary higher direct image [pqf-def-cohomology], and module restriction [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. There exist natural transformations in O_X-modules c_V:H^p(U,(-)|_U), with its scalar action forgotten, →Γ(V,R^p f_*(-)). For every O_X-module N [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every injective resolution I of N [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and every V, put K=f_*I. There is an isomorphism of additive groups e:H^p(U,N|_U)→(sectionCohomologyPresheaf K p)(V). The component c_V(N) equals e.hom followed by the value at V of sectionCohomologyTheta K p, and then of the underlying module map (I.isoRightDerivedObj f_* p).inv. There is no affine-basis morphism detection assertion.

source.place: Lemma 20.7.3 and Lemma 20.7.1 (01E1); coefficient naturality of the resolution comparison

proof.text: Apply the fully proved natural open-restriction comparison to each U=f⁻¹V. Choose its natural isomorphism a_V; its existence is proved by an actual restricted resolution and homology comparison, not by a new unproved existence statement.

Construct the comparison on derived open sections using the concrete resolution section map on Mathlib chosen resolutions. The fixed resolution naturality equality makes its components a natural transformation. Apply the same equality to the identity coefficient map between a chosen resolution and arbitrary I; functors preserve identity maps, so the components agree for every I.

Compose a_V.hom with this natural transformation. For N and I take e to be a_V(N), followed by I.isoRightDerivedObj for open sections and exact evaluation mapHomologyIso for the section cohomology presheaf. This is an actual composite of isomorphisms. The arbitrary-resolution formula from the preceding step and associativity give the required component identity.

theorem higherDirectImage_coefficient_comparison
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ∀ V : Y.Opens,
      Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ⋙
        RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace p ⋙
          forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u}
            ((moduleRings (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))
              AddCommGrpCat.{u} ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p ⋙
        RingedSpace.openModuleSections Y.toRingedSpace V,
      ∀ (N : X.Modules) (I : InjectiveResolution
        (show SheafOfModules (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) from N)) (V : Y.Opens),
        let K := ((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex
        ∃ e :
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ⋙
            RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace p ⋙
              forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u}
                ((moduleRings (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))
                  AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj N) ≅
            (Scheme.Modules.sectionCohomologyPresheaf K p).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op V),
          (c V).app N = e.hom ≫
            ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).obj).map
              (Scheme.Modules.sectionCohomologyTheta K p ≫
                (SheafOfModules.forget (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)).map
                  (I.isoRightDerivedObj
                    (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom) p).inv)).app
                      (Opposite.op V)
